statement: Fix a matrix norm bound. For the covariance conclusion, assume positive margins in (13.1) and suppose that every point in its small-residual region has q(y) ≥ c∗ > 0. On the fixed-length ordinary and restricted inverse-word events specified below, ∥ Covµh (G, X)∥ ≤ C ( Varµh (G) + Dh(G) )1/2 for every G. In particular ∥Σh∥ ≤ C. For the following mean conclusion, only the whole-region root stability implication ∥Fh(y)∥ ≤ ρ0 √ n =⇒ H(y, Vy) ⪰ c0I is required, together with ordinary word diagnostics. No lower bound on q(y) is assumed in this mean conclusion. For N = µh(f2) > 0 and νh = f2µh/N, and each sufficiently small fixed ζ > 0, ∥Eνh X − Eµh X∥ √ n ≤ Cζ + Cζ √ n ( 1 + Dh(f) N ) . (13.2) The leading constant C depends on the fixed norm and stability margins, but not on ζ. Without the stability hypothesis, put Qδ(h) = sup ∥Fh(y)∥≤δ √ n q(y), with an empty supremum equal to zero. The same ordinary diagnostics give ∥Eνh X − Eµh X∥ √ n ≤ 2 q Qδ(h) + Cδ √ n ( 1 + Dh(f) N ) . (13.3) For each fixed δ > 0 this assertion holds for sufficiently large n on the corresponding ordinary diagnostics. All events are independent of f, G and the unit directions used to test these inequalities.
